title: Boot device registry
statement: The device registry shall accept unique boot-defined names and static driver objects before sealing at scheduler start.
rationale: Drivers currently require single-owner integration without a common registry.
acceptance: Duplicate names, null operation tables, capacity overflow and post-start registration fail unchanged; lookup returns the exact registered instance or not-found.
verification: Registry capacity, duplicate, seal and lookup tests.
configuration: Optional devices; positive maximum device count; names at most 31 bytes.
resource_budget: Fixed registry entries and copied bounded names; zero runtime allocation.
finding: Driver guidance reserves objects statically but no device registry API exists.

title: Unified device operations
statement: Devices shall expose bounded read, write and typed control operations returning status and transferred byte count, with explicit nonblocking or absolute-deadline modes.
rationale: A consistent contract avoids per-driver ambiguity and indefinite calls.
acceptance: Unsupported operations return not-supported; zero-length operations transfer zero; short transfers report exact progress; expired deadlines never wait; control rejects unknown commands and incorrect payload sizes unchanged.
verification: Mock-driver short transfer, unsupported, deadline and control validation tests.
configuration: Fixed operation table per device; finite control command set.
resource_budget: Caller buffers only; request state bounded by configured concurrent operations.
finding: Ethernet has explicit busy/error callback contracts but no general read/write/control interface exists.

title: Bounded descriptor handles
statement: Opening a device or file shall acquire a slot from a boot-reserved descriptor table and return an index-plus-generation handle.
rationale: Unix-style handles need finite capacity and stale-reference protection.
acceptance: Exactly configured slot count opens succeed; excess returns resource-exhausted; close/reopen invalidates old handles; generations never wrap into reuse because exhausted-generation slots retire until reboot.
verification: Exhaustion, stale handle, invalid index and near-generation-limit tests.
configuration: Optional descriptors; configured slot count; 32-bit generation.
resource_budget: Fixed descriptor records; no heap; retired slots remain counted unavailable.
finding: Current API exposes Thread pointers only; no descriptor table or generation management exists.

title: Descriptor close lifecycle
statement: Close shall mark a valid descriptor closing, reject new operations, wait only until its supplied deadline for in-flight operations and release the slot exactly once after quiescence.
rationale: Freeing slots during active driver access would corrupt ownership.
acceptance: Double close returns invalid-handle; timed close returns timeout while retaining closing state; resumed close completes after drain; driver-close failure preserves a diagnosable unavailable slot.
verification: Close versus read/write races, timeout retry and injected close-failure tests.
configuration: Finite per-slot active-operation counter; close uses absolute deadline.
resource_budget: Fixed closing state and active count per descriptor; no detached cleanup allocation.
finding: Existing ownership guidance does not define descriptor teardown or concurrent close.

title: Bounded pathname resolution
statement: The VFS shall resolve absolute bounded paths with collapsed repeated separators and dot components, rejecting parent traversal above root and all symbolic links.
rationale: A small namespace must avoid recursive and unbounded resolution.
acceptance: Overlong paths/components fail before provider calls; /a/../b resolves /b; /../b fails invalid-path; relative paths and embedded null payloads are rejected; no symlink following occurs.
verification: Path normalization model and malformed/boundary input tests.
configuration: Optional VFS; positive maximum path bytes, component bytes and component count.
resource_budget: Fixed normalization workspace per configured concurrent resolver; traversal bounded by component count.
finding: No pathname API or VFS configuration exists; static memory rules require bounded resolver workspace.

title: Static device filesystem
statement: A devfs provider shall expose sealed device-registry entries under /dev and route opens through descriptor ownership rules.
rationale: The accepted Unix-style device namespace should reuse registry identity.
acceptance: Every registered exported device appears once; unknown names return not-found; directory iteration is bounded and stable; create, unlink and rename return read-only.
verification: Registry-to-devfs mapping, stable enumeration and forbidden mutation tests.
configuration: Optional devfs; boot export flag per device.
resource_budget: No duplicated driver objects; at most one fixed directory record per exported device.
finding: Drivers are listed in documentation but /dev has no implementation.

title: Read-only ROM filesystem
statement: A ROM filesystem shall expose a boot-linked immutable file table with bounded offset reads and no executable loading.
rationale: Static assets and help text need file access without writable storage complexity.
acceptance: Reads at EOF return zero; short tail reads are exact; overflowing offsets and invalid table ranges fail; all writes and namespace mutations return read-only; content bytes match linked assets.
verification: ROM image table validation, offset boundaries and content checksum tests.
configuration: Optional ROMFS; fixed file count and linked asset byte budget.
resource_budget: Immutable table and linked bytes; per-open offset stored in descriptor slot.
finding: The linker builds one static firmware image; no filesystem or executable loader exists.

title: Bounded RAM filesystem
statement: Optional RAMFS shall use boot-reserved inode and data-block pools, permit only regular files and directories and return explicit exhaustion without growing storage.
rationale: Writable temporary files must preserve the no-heap contract.
acceptance: Inode/block exhaustion leaves existing contents intact; writes may return documented exact short counts; unlink of open files reclaims blocks only after last close; truncate zeroes newly visible bytes; reboot discards contents.
verification: Pool exhaustion, short write, open-unlink, truncate and repeated create/delete conservation tests.
configuration: Optional RAMFS; fixed inode count, block size, block count and directory-entry capacity.
resource_budget: Exactly configured inode, directory and block pools; ownership counters conserve every slot.
finding: Memory helpers exist but no writable filesystem or fixed block ownership manager exists.

title: Boot mount table
statement: Mounts shall be registered only at boot with unique absolute normalized prefixes, then remain immutable; resolution shall select the longest component-boundary prefix.
rationale: Immutable mounting keeps lookup and provider lifetime bounded.
acceptance: Duplicate prefixes and mount-table overflow fail; /rom does not match /romance; nested mount chooses longest match; runtime mount/unmount returns sealed.
verification: Prefix boundary, nested mount, duplicate, capacity and boot seal tests.
configuration: Fixed mount count; optional devfs, ROMFS and RAMFS providers.
resource_budget: Fixed mount table and bounded copied prefixes; lookup scans at most configured mounts.
finding: There are no current mount options; configuration guidance requires lifecycle and budgets before exposure.

title: Static byte pipes
statement: A pipe shall use a boot-reserved byte ring and bounded endpoint slots, provide partial FIFO transfers and resolve endpoint closure without dynamic allocation.
rationale: Pipes provide useful Unix-style composition without processes.
acceptance: Empty pipe with writers returns would-block or waits to deadline; empty pipe without writers returns EOF; write without readers returns broken-pipe; close wakes affected waiters; byte order survives ring wrap.
verification: Ring wrap, full/empty, deadline, endpoint-close races and endpoint exhaustion tests.
configuration: Optional pipes; fixed pipe count, bytes per pipe and reader/writer endpoint limits.
resource_budget: Fixed rings and endpoint records; total queued bytes never exceeds configured storage.
finding: No pipe API exists; static byte storage and exact endpoint teardown must be added.

title: Built-in command registry
statement: The shell shall dispatch only a sealed boot-defined table of built-in C++ command functions with unique bounded names.
rationale: A Unix-like console need not load programs or create processes.
acceptance: Duplicate/overlong names fail at boot; unknown commands return command-not-found; dispatch invokes only registered pointers; registry overflow fails unchanged.
verification: Registry validation, unknown command and dispatch identity tests.
configuration: Optional shell; fixed command count and maximum command-name bytes.
resource_budget: Fixed command table; all command code linked into firmware.
finding: Firmware is statically linked and no shell registry or process loader exists.

title: Bounded shell parser
statement: The shell shall parse bounded lines with whitespace separation, single/double quoted arguments and backslash escapes, rejecting unsupported expansion, redirection and pipeline syntax initially.
rationale: Explicit small grammar avoids accidental unbounded Unix-shell expectations.
acceptance: Overlong line, too many arguments, unmatched quotes, trailing escape and unsupported syntax return parse errors without command execution; quoted spaces and empty arguments preserve exact bytes.
verification: Grammar corpus, boundary tests and deterministic fuzzing against reference parser.
configuration: Fixed maximum line bytes and argument count; no environment expansion or command substitution.
resource_budget: One fixed line buffer and argument-index array per shell session.
finding: No parser exists; caller-owned storage policy rules out dynamically growing argument vectors.

title: Static shell sessions
statement: Each enabled shell session shall own boot-reserved input/output buffers and a boot-created worker, with bounded editing and output backpressure.
rationale: Console convenience must not consume unbounded kernel memory or stall unrelated threads.
acceptance: Session capacity is fixed; line overflow discards until newline and reports one error; output waits only to deadline and reports truncation; disconnected sessions release no borrowed buffer prematurely.
verification: Maximum sessions, oversized line recovery, slow output and disconnect tests.
configuration: Fixed session count, worker priority/stack and input/output ring bytes.
resource_budget: Exactly configured session buffers and stacks; no runtime worker creation.
finding: Current kernel seals thread creation at start, so interactive sessions require boot-created workers.

title: Jobs on boot workers
statement: Background commands shall run only on a fixed boot-created worker pool with generation-tagged job slots and cooperative cancellation.
rationale: Provide limited jobs without fork, executable loading or runtime stacks.
acceptance: Pool exhaustion returns busy; completed slots invalidate stale job IDs; cancellation requests never forcibly unwind stacks; noncooperating jobs remain occupied and are reported stuck after configured deadline.
verification: Pool exhaustion, stale IDs, completion/cancel races and noncooperating-job tests.
configuration: Optional jobs; fixed worker/job count, stacks and cancellation grace ticks.
resource_budget: One permanent stack/control block per worker plus fixed job records and bounded copied arguments.
finding: create is boot-only and exit does not unwind active objects; background work cannot safely imply dynamic tasks or forced cancellation.

title: Bounded diagnostic commands
statement: Built-in ps, top, uptime and devices commands shall consume coherent bounded snapshots and print explicit truncation indicators without holding kernel locks during formatting or output.
rationale: Existing thread metrics should become usable from the console without long masked I/O.
acceptance: ps reports name/state/base/effective priority; top handles zero elapsed time and disabled metrics explicitly; rows never exceed caller capacity; slow console output occurs after snapshot lock release.
verification: Snapshot-to-command golden outputs, truncation, disabled metrics and slow-console instrumentation.
configuration: Optional diagnostics; fixed maximum rows and output bytes per command invocation.
resource_budget: Fixed snapshot rows and formatting buffer per session; one snapshot per refresh.
finding: snapshot already returns bounded rows and priority/runtime fields; no shell commands or base/effective split exists.

title: UART bounded transport
statement: The UART driver shall use fixed RX/TX rings, expose nonblocking/deadline transfers and defer interrupt processing through approved bounded paths.
rationale: UART is the documented first board addition and console prerequisite.
acceptance: RX overflow drops newest byte and increments a saturating counter; TX full returns short count or waits only to deadline; framing/parity/overrun errors are counted; loopback preserves accepted byte order.
verification: Hardware/model loopback, ring saturation, error injection and deadline tests.
configuration: Optional UART instances; fixed ring bytes, baud and framing selected at boot.
resource_budget: Fixed per-instance rings/control state; ISR work capped at configured bytes per interrupt.
finding: Driver inventory proposes UART rings and loopback tests; no UART implementation exists.

title: Console routing and fault output
statement: Console input/output shall route to one boot-selected device; panic output shall use a bounded polling path with a fixed byte/time limit and no descriptor locks.
rationale: Diagnostics must remain bounded when scheduler or locks fail.
acceptance: Normal output follows device backpressure; panic writes at most configured bytes and stops at deadline or unavailable device; recursive panic terminates immediately without lock acquisition.
verification: Slow/stuck UART, recursive panic and scheduler-disabled output tests.
configuration: One boot console; optional panic output with positive byte and tick/cycle limits.
resource_budget: Fixed panic buffer and recursion flag; no worker or memory acquisition in panic.
finding: stop currently disables interrupts and loops; no console routing or bounded emergency output exists.

title: GPIO ownership and safe state
statement: GPIO shall enforce boot-declared pin ownership, validated direction/functions and board-defined safe output values on failed initialization or explicit shutdown.
rationale: Uncoordinated register access can affect unrelated pins and unsafe outputs.
acceptance: Conflicting claims and unsupported pin/function fail before hardware changes; writes affect only owned pins; output values are established before enabling drive; failure restores declared safe state.
verification: Mock-register ownership/mask tests and board safe-state measurements.
configuration: Optional fixed pin table and owner map; board safe values required for outputs.
resource_budget: One fixed record per declared pin; no runtime pin claims.
finding: Inventory requests pin ownership and atomic register semantics but no GPIO contract is implemented.

title: SPI bounded transactions
statement: SPI shall accept transactions from fixed boot request slots, serialize each bus and hold chip select only for one bounded transaction with an absolute completion deadline.
rationale: Bus sharing and chip-select lifetime require explicit ownership.
acceptance: Validate mode/rate/length before assertion; preserve segment order; queue full returns busy; timeout deasserts chip select and returns transferred count; subsequent requests recover or receive unavailable.
verification: Mode validation, contention, full queue, timeout and chip-select waveform tests.
configuration: Optional buses; fixed request count, maximum segments/bytes and supported rates/modes.
resource_budget: Fixed request/control slots and configured DMA buffers; no retained stack buffer beyond synchronous call.
finding: SPI inventory lists slots, chip-select ownership and timeouts without an implemented driver.

title: I2C error and recovery bounds
statement: I2C shall serialize bounded address transactions, report NACK/arbitration/timeout distinctly and attempt at most nine recovery clocks followed by STOP before marking a stuck bus unavailable.
rationale: A stuck peripheral must not block a worker indefinitely.
acceptance: Invalid addresses/lengths fail before START; repeated-start sequences preserve atomic ownership; NACK returns exact progress; recovery is attempted once per failed transaction and never exceeds deadline; unavailable buses reject requests until explicit bounded reinitialize.
verification: NACK, arbitration loss, clock stretch, stuck SDA and recovery waveform tests.
configuration: Optional buses; fixed request count/bytes; standard 7-bit addressing initially.
resource_budget: Fixed transaction slots and one bus recovery state per instance.
finding: I2C inventory identifies NACK/stuck-bus concerns but defines no recovery bound or implementation.

title: Progress-based watchdog supervision
statement: A boot-created supervisor shall feed the hardware watchdog only when every enabled critical thread advances its registered progress token within its configured monotonic interval.
rationale: Timer interrupts alone do not demonstrate application progress.
acceptance: A stuck critical worker prevents feeding by its deadline; token wrap is handled; noncritical workers do not inhibit feeding; first missed participant is recorded before reset; watchdog setup is validated against supervisor period.
verification: Stalled worker, interrupt-only activity, token wrap, false-positive margin and actual reset tests.
configuration: Optional supervisor; fixed critical participant list and positive per-participant deadlines.
resource_budget: Fixed token/deadline records plus one boot supervisor stack; one scan per supervision period.
finding: Documentation recommends progress-based feeding and reset records; no supervisor or watchdog driver exists.

title: Ordered driver boot failure
statement: Drivers shall initialize from a fixed dependency-ordered boot table; failure shall disable transitive dependents and unwind successfully initialized affected devices in reverse order to safe state.
rationale: Partial initialization must not leave workers using unavailable hardware.
acceptance: Cycle/unknown dependency fails before hardware access; init order follows dependencies; injected failure prevents dependent initialization; reverse shutdown is called once; critical failure prevents scheduler start while optional failure is exposed diagnostically.
verification: Dependency graph validation and failure injection at every boot-table position.
configuration: Fixed init entry count; critical/optional classification and bounded init/shutdown deadlines.
resource_budget: Fixed table and visited/state arrays; traversal bounded by configured entries/edges.
finding: Boot/recovery backlog proposes ordered init and partial-start tests but start has no driver dependency orchestration.

title: Device request cancellation
statement: Timed device operations shall transfer buffer ownership back only after hardware/DMA access has stopped; unsuccessful abort shall quarantine the fixed request slot and return a distinct fault result.
rationale: Timeout alone cannot make asynchronous buffer reuse safe.
acceptance: Successful timeout/abort proves device ownership revoked before return; failed abort retains driver-owned fixed buffers and quarantines slot; late completions cannot target reused generation; repeated abort is idempotent.
verification: Delayed DMA completion, abort success/failure, stale completion and slot quarantine tests.
configuration: Fixed abort deadline and request-generation width; asynchronous drivers use driver-owned buffers.
resource_budget: Fixed request slots and staging buffers; quarantined capacity never silently reused.
finding: Ethernet explicitly forbids retaining caller TX pointers; broader timed/DMA operation cancellation is unspecified.

title: Bounded readiness polling
statement: A readiness API shall inspect a bounded caller-supplied descriptor set for read/write/error readiness and wait atomically to a deadline without consuming data.
rationale: Shell and worker loops need multiplexing without polling every device indefinitely.
acceptance: Oversized sets fail before driver calls; already-ready returns immediately; readiness transition between registration and sleep is not lost; closed/stale handles report per-entry error; timeout returns zero ready entries.
verification: Ready-before-wait, transition race, close race, invalid handle and maximum-set tests.
configuration: Optional readiness; configured maximum descriptors per wait.
resource_budget: One boot-reserved readiness record per waiting thread and bounded descriptor indices.
finding: Current yield/sleep APIs provide no multi-device readiness mechanism or atomic readiness wait.

title: Coherent device diagnostics
statement: Each driver shall expose a bounded typed health snapshot containing availability, fault reason, capacity/occupancy, overflow/error counts and reset generation without clearing counters on read.
rationale: Operators need to distinguish absent hardware, resource exhaustion and driver faults.
acceptance: Snapshots are internally coherent; counters saturate at maximum rather than wrap; repeated reads have no reset side effect; disabled features return not-supported; fixed output truncation reports required/written rows.
verification: Concurrent update/snapshot, saturation, disabled driver and bounded enumeration tests.
configuration: Optional device metrics with fixed per-driver schema and maximum snapshot rows.
resource_budget: Fixed per-device counters/state and caller-owned snapshot rows; no formatting under driver locks.
finding: Ethernet exposes unsynchronized owner-thread counters while thread snapshot reports required/written rows; no unified device health snapshot exists.
